title: ReefMappeR
text: ReefMappeR provides streamlined workflow researchers students working reef ecosystem data. Starting bounding box Sentinel-2 satellite image, package automatically loads crops bathymetry, benthic habitat, geomorphology, seagrass data area interest produces habitat maps, depth statistics, water quality assessments, change detection outputs Normalized Difference Chlorophyll Index (NDCI) Total Suspended Sediments (TSS). Benthic habitats geomorphic zones Whitsundays region, Great Barrier Reef.

what: Calculate Normalized Difference Chlorophyll Index (NDCI) — calc_ndci
title: Calculate Normalized Difference Chlorophyll Index (NDCI) — calc_ndci
text: Computes NDCI Sentinel-2 image using red (B4) red-edge (B5) bands. NDCI spectral index designed highlight chlorophyll-concentration turbid, productive coastal inland waters. uses normalized difference red-edge (705 nm) red (665 nm) reflectance water particularly sensitive phytoplankton chlorophyll.

title: Calculate Normalized Difference Chlorophyll Index (NDCI) — calc_ndci
code: calc_ndci(s2, red_name = NULL, rededge_name = NULL, verbose = TRUE)

title: Calculate Normalized Difference Chlorophyll Index (NDCI) — calc_ndci
text: s2 SpatRaster Sentinel-2 image containing least B4 (red) B5 (red-edge) bands. red_name Character name red band. NULL, auto-detects "B4", "B04", "red". rededge_name Character name red-edge band. NULL, auto-detects "B5", "B05", "rededge". verbose Logical; print available band names inspection.

title: Calculate Normalized Difference Chlorophyll Index (NDCI) — calc_ndci
text: SpatRaster single NDCI layer (values -1 1).

title: Calculate Normalized Difference Chlorophyll Index (NDCI) — calc_ndci
text: NDCI calculated : $$NDCI = \frac{B5 - B4}{B5 + B4}$$ Value interpretation: -1 0: Low chlorophyll-, clear water non-productive conditions 0 0.3: Moderate chlorophyll-, typical coastal waters >0.3: High chlorophyll-, potential eutrophication algal blooms Exact chlorophyll-concentrations require site-specific calibration -situ measurements. #' @references Mishra, S. & Mishra, D.R. (2012). Normalized difference chlorophyll index: novel model remote sensing chlorophyll-concentration turbid productive waters. Remote Sensing Environment, 117, 394–406. doi:10.1016/j.rse.2011.10.016

title: Calculate Normalized Difference Chlorophyll Index (NDCI) — calc_ndci
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Auto-detect bands (works with B4/B5 or B04/B05 naming) ndci <- calc_ndci(s2) plot(ndci)  # Explicit band names ndci <- calc_ndci(s2, red_name = "B4", rededge_name = "B5") } # }

title: Assess reef change between two NDCI rasters — assess_reef_change
text: ndci_t1 SpatRaster. NDCI time 1, output calc_ndci(). ndci_t2 SpatRaster. NDCI time 2, output calc_ndci().

title: Assess reef change between two NDCI rasters — assess_reef_change
text: SpatRaster pixel-wise difference (t2 minus t1). Positive values indicate increase, negative values decrease. Pass result compare_ndci_change() compare_tss_change() visualisation.

title: Assess reef change between two NDCI rasters — assess_reef_change
text: NDCI difference calculated : $$\Delta NDCI = NDCI_{t2} - NDCI_{t1}$$ two rasters share geometry, ndci_t2 automatically resampled match ndci_t1 using bilinear interpolation. meaningful change detection, images season minimise phenological differences, pre-processed surface reflectance (Sentinel-2 Level-2A).

title: Assess reef change between two NDCI rasters — assess_reef_change
text: Mishra, S. & Mishra, D.R. (2012). Normalized difference chlorophyll index: novel model remote sensing chlorophyll-concentration turbid productive waters. Remote Sensing Environment, 117, 394–406. doi:10.1016/j.rse.2011.10.016

title: Assess reef change between two NDCI rasters — assess_reef_change
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ s2_24  <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "Sentinel2_2024_example.tif",                                    package = "ReefMappeR")) s2_25  <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "Sentinel2_example.tif",                                    package = "ReefMappeR")) change <- assess_reef_change(calc_ndci(s2_24), calc_ndci(s2_25)) compare_habitats_change(change) } # }

what: Calculate Total Suspended Sediments (TSS) from Sentinel-2 — calculate_water_quality
title: Calculate Total Suspended Sediments (TSS) from Sentinel-2 — calculate_water_quality
text: Estimates Total Suspended Sediments (TSS) Sentinel-2 Level-2A surface reflectance image using red/green band ratio algorithm. NIR-based water mask applied exclude land non-water pixels.

title: Calculate Total Suspended Sediments (TSS) from Sentinel-2 — calculate_water_quality
code: calculate_water_quality(s2)

title: Calculate Total Suspended Sediments (TSS) from Sentinel-2 — calculate_water_quality
text: s2 terra::SpatRaster object containing least bands "B3" (green), "B4" (red), "B8" (NIR) Sentinel-2 Level-2A product (surface reflectance, values 0–10000).

title: Calculate Total Suspended Sediments (TSS) from Sentinel-2 — calculate_water_quality
text: SpatRaster estimated TSS g/m\(^3\), masked water pixels . plot displayed automatically.

title: Calculate Total Suspended Sediments (TSS) from Sentinel-2 — calculate_water_quality
text: TSS derived red/green reflectance relationship form $$TSS = 1.47 \times (R_{red} / R_{green}) + 31.4 \times R_{red},$$ \(R_{red}\) \(R_{green}\) surface reflectances Sentinel-2 bands B4 B3 respectively, scaled 0–1. Negative values set zero. simple water mask applied using band B8 (NIR) threshold 0.05; pixels threshold treated non-water set NA. algorithm generic coastal-water approximation locally validated recalibrated -situ measurements use quantitative analyses.

title: Calculate Total Suspended Sediments (TSS) from Sentinel-2 — calculate_water_quality
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ s2 <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "Sentinel2_example.tif",                                package = "ReefMappeR")) tss <- calculate_water_quality(s2) } # }

text: Crops bathymetry (GEBCO), benthic habitats, geomorphology (Allen Coral Atlas), seagrass datasets extent Sentinel-2 image bounding box. Benthic geomorphic data mosaicked native ~10 m resolution; GEBCO bathymetry resampled onto ACA grid.

title: Crop datasets to a specified region of interest — set_roi
text: s2 SpatRaster. Sentinel-2 image defining ROI. spatial extent used. Optional, provide either s2 bbox. bathymetry SpatRaster. NULL, loads GEBCO_2024 extdata. benthic SpatRaster. NULL, auto-loads matching Allen Coral Atlas tiles. geomorph SpatRaster. NULL, auto-loads matching Allen Coral Atlas tiles. seagrass SpatVector. NULL, loads bundled GBR seagrass dataset. bbox Numeric vector c(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) sf/sfc object defining ROI. Optional, alternative s2.

title: Temporal NDCI Change Classification — compare_habitats_change
text: Classifies pixel-wise NDCI change three categories: increase chlorophyll-, significant change, decrease chlorophyll-.

title: Temporal NDCI Change Classification — compare_habitats_change
code: compare_habitats_change(ndci_change, threshold = 0.1)

title: Temporal NDCI Change Classification — compare_habitats_change
text: ndci_change SpatRaster. Output assess_reef_change(). threshold Numeric. Minimum absolute NDCI change considered significant. Default 0.1. See Details.

title: Temporal NDCI Change Classification — compare_habitats_change
text: Invisible NULL. Called side effects (plot).

title: Temporal NDCI Change Classification — compare_habitats_change
text: NDCI change classified three classes: Chl-increase (NDCI change > +threshold): Indicates elevated phytoplankton biomass, potentially associated eutrophication, algal blooms, increased nutrient input. significant change (|NDCI change| <= threshold): Change within defined threshold, interpreted natural variability sensor noise rather ecologically meaningful signal. Chl-decrease (NDCI change < -threshold): Indicates reduced phytoplankton biomass, potentially reflecting improved water clarity reduced nutrient availability. default threshold 0.1 practical convention used exploratory NDCI change analyses site-specific calibration data available. treated starting point adjusted based local conditions sensor characteristics. universally established threshold exists literature; Mishra & Mishra (2012) demonstrate NDCI can qualitatively map chlorophyll-without -situ data, define change threshold. robust trend analysis across multiple time points, statistical approaches Mann-Kendall trend test recommended (European Environment Agency, 2024).

title: Getting Started with ReefMappeR
text: ReefMappeR R package mapping analysing reef habitats Great Barrier Reef (GBR) using satellite remote sensing open marine datasets. integrates four data sources single, reproducible workflow: GEBCO 2024 bathymetry — global seafloor depth model ~450 m resolution Allen Coral Atlas — high-resolution (5 m) benthic habitat geomorphic zone maps derived PlanetScope satellite imagery machine learning UNEP-WCMC seagrass polygons — global seagrass distribution database Sentinel-2 Level-2A satellite imagery — multispectral imagery 10 m resolution water quality analysis package designed researchers students want rapidly characterise reef habitats, assess water quality, detect temporal change without manual data processing.

title: Getting Started with ReefMappeR
text: Sentinel-2 European Space Agency (ESA) satellite mission providing free, open-access multispectral imagery 10 m spatial resolution revisit time approximately 5 days. reef monitoring offers several advantages: 10 m resolution — sufficient delineate benthic features reef structures Red-edge band (B5, 705 nm) — sensitive chlorophyll-concentration, enabling NDCI calculation Free open access — available via Copernicus Open Access Hub Level-2A products — atmospherically corrected surface reflectance, ready water quality analysis vignette use two Sentinel-2 Level-2A images Tongue Reef, GBR, acquired summer 2024 summer 2025.

title: Getting Started with ReefMappeR
text: calc_ndci() computes Normalized Difference Chlorophyll Index (NDCI) Sentinel-2 bands B4 (665 nm, red) B5 (705 nm, red-edge). NDCI proxy chlorophyll-concentration — primary photosynthetic pigment phytoplankton algae. Elevated chlorophyll-reefs can indicate eutrophication terrestrial runoff, significant threat coral reef ecosystems (Mishra & Mishra, 2012). NDCI values range -1 +1: < 0: low chlorophyll-, clear oligotrophic water 0–0.3: moderate chlorophyll-, typical coastal conditions > 0.3: high chlorophyll-, potential eutrophication algal bloom
code: s2   <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "Sentinel2_example.tif",                                  package = "ReefMappeR")) ndci <- calc_ndci(s2)

title: Getting Started with ReefMappeR
text: calculate_water_quality() estimates Total Suspended Sediments (TSS) g/m³ Sentinel-2 bands B3 (green), B4 (red), B8 (NIR). TSS key indicator water turbidity — high sediment loads reduce light availability corals seagrass can cause physical smothering reef communities.
code: tss <- calculate_water_quality(s2)

title: Getting Started with ReefMappeR
text: assess_reef_change() computes pixel-wise difference two rasters (t2 minus t1). Applied NDCI, positive values indicate increased chlorophyll-two dates — potentially reflecting worsening water quality increased algal growth. Negative values indicate improved water clarity. compare_ndci_change() classifies change three categories using user-defined threshold (default ±0.1):
code: s2_24   <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "Sentinel2_2024_example.tif",                                     package = "ReefMappeR")) s2_25   <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "Sentinel2_example.tif",                                     package = "ReefMappeR")) ndci_24 <- calc_ndci(s2_24) ndci_25 <- calc_ndci(s2_25)  change_ndci <- assess_reef_change(ndci_24, ndci_25) compare_ndci_change(change_ndci)

title: Getting Started with ReefMappeR
text: Applied TSS, assess_reef_change() reveals changes suspended sediment load. Increased TSS may reflect storm events, dredging activity, intensified terrestrial runoff. compare_tss_change() classifies change using threshold ±0.5 g/m³ default.
code: tss_24 <- calculate_water_quality(s2_24) tss_25 <- calculate_water_quality(s2_25)  change_tss <- assess_reef_change(tss_24, tss_25) compare_tss_change(change_tss)
